questions.stem: A known gangster was admitted to emergency after a shootout with police personnel. An inquiry was started to investigate police encounters. In gun-shot wound, distance assessment is done from:

options.label: A
options.text: Entry wound without singeing and tattooing

options.label: B
options.text: Number of pellets

options.label: C
options.text: Colour of wound

options.label: D
options.text: Size of wound

questions.answerText: Entry wound without singeing and tattooing
questions.solutionHtml:
Entry wound without singeing and tattooing
  • The number of pellets and the Colour of the wound are not related to the distance of the firearm weapon from the victim. The size of the wound has only a limited relationship with the distance of the firearm weapon; in any case not reliable.
  • When we say that the 'Entry wound without singeing and tattooing' means that the distance of the firearm weapon at the time of discharge is more than the range of tattooing,e., more than 60 cm.

questions.stem: A surgeon was exploring a gunshot wound on the chest. Police personnel informed the surgeon about the faulty gun. In tandem bullets, the number of bullets fired is:
questions.solutionHtml:
2
  • In tandem bullets, the number of shots fired is two. Tandem Bullet or piggyback bullet (tandem = one behind the other)- Occasionally, more bullets are found than the number of entrance wounds.
  • This occurs due to defects in the weapon, faulty ammunition, or a loaded firearm that has been unused for several years.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 212 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 177

questions.stemHtml: A 28-year-old male, while returning home after completing his work, was caught by a few thieves. They were trying to snatch things from him, and during the fight, he was being shot by the thieves. He was dead by the time he was taken to the hospital. During the autopsy examination, the following finding was noted. Which of the following statement about the type of firearm used is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a wound which is caused by a shotgun that is rifled

options.label: B
options.text: The range from which the gun was fired was around 1 m.

options.label: C
options.text: The essential projectile element in this type of gun is pellets.

options.label: D
options.text: In this type of gun, the diameter is measured by the distance between two opposite lands.

questions.answerText: The essential projectile element in this type of gun is pellets.
questions.solutionHtml:
The essential projectile element in this type of gun is pellets.

In the given question, the type of firearm used in this is a shotgun. In a short gun, the cartridge consists of pellets and not bullets.




KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd Edition, Page Number- 212 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 164-168

questions.stemHtml: While reading the chapter on forensic ballistic, you came across the following figure as given below. What are this phenomenon known as, and what is its advantage?

options.label: A
options.text: Rifling- it provides the advantage of spinning effect to the projectile.

options.label: B
options.text: Musket- the end of the firearm is narrowed to provide it with more compactness.

options.label: C
options.text: Choking- narrowing the gun's terminal part to improve the pellets' velocity and explosive power.

options.label: D
options.text: None of these.

questions.answerText: Choking- narrowing the gun's terminal part to improve the pellets' velocity and explosive power.
questions.solutionHtml:
Choking- narrowing the gun's terminal part to improve the pellets' velocity and explosive power.
  • In the given image, the terminal part of the gun is narrowed.
  • This is known as choking. It offers the following advantages-
    • Choking lessens the rate of spread of the shot after it leaves the muzzle.
    • Increases the explosive force and increases the velocity



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd Edition, Page Number- 210 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 160

questions.stem: The cartridge of shotguns is unique in the sense they consist of wads. Wads offer the following advantage-

options.label: A
options.text: Provide compact packing to the pellet and the gunpowder compartment.

options.label: B
options.text: Prevent the leakage of gases so that they can act as a piston.

options.label: C
options.text: Prevent shock absorption or cushion.

options.label: D
options.text: Prevent the leakage of heat or transfer to the pellet compartment.

questions.solutionHtml:
Prevent shock absorption or cushion.
  • The cartridge of the shotgun consists of the wad, which is made up of cork material or plastic.
  • Wad acts as a cushion or shock absorber. So, wad doesn’t prevent shock absorption.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd Edition, Page Number- 213 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 161,162

questions.stem: You were posted in an emergency when a 45 year old male was brought by a passer by as he has suffered gunshot injury. The patient was vitally unstable and was managed by resuscitation. You have called a forensic medicine expert to evaluate the wound. He, after examining explains to you that the wound explains a greater range of firing than it was. In which phenomena does this happens?

options.label: A
options.text: Welding of shot

options.label: B
options.text: Billiard ball effect

options.label: C
options.text: Internal ricochet

options.label: D
options.text: None of the above.

questions.solutionHtml:
Billiard ball effect
  • In the given question, as described, the range of the shot appeared to be more than the This occurs in billiard ball ricochet phenomena.
  • At close range, while the shots are bunched, they strike one another upon impact on the primary target, i.e., the skin or clothes, and spread out in a wide pattern as they pass through the body. This causes the shot to spread widely and may suggest a greater range of fire than occurred.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd Edition, Page Number- 220 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 168
